title_en: Suzhou Dongbao Real Estate Co., Ltd., Suzhou Jincheng Guarantee Co., Ltd., Suzhou Dongbao Metal Materials Co., Ltd., Suzhou Dongbao Youhei Metal Materials Co., Ltd., and Xu Ada v. Suzhou General Merchandise Company and Jiangsu Shaonv Zhichun Group Company — dispute over asset transfer contract
ruling_gist_en: 1. Where parties have entered into multiple contracts, some of which contain an arbitration clause, while others neither contain an arbitration clause nor are explicitly listed as annexes to the contracts containing the arbitration clause, nor indicate acceptance of the arbitration jurisdiction clause in the contracts containing the arbitration clause. Although there is a certain degree of correlation between the above-mentioned contracts, their respective independence cannot be denied on this ground.

full_text_en:
Suzhou Dongbao Real Estate Co., Ltd., Suzhou Jincheng Guarantee Co., Ltd., Suzhou Dongbao Metal Materials Co., Ltd., Suzhou Dongbao Ferrous Metal Materials Co., Ltd., and Xu Ada v. Suzhou General Merchandise Corporation and Jiangsu Girl's Spring Group — dispute over asset transfer contract

Ruling Summary

1. Where multiple contracts are executed between the parties, some may contain an arbitration clause, while others may neither provide for an arbitration clause nor expressly incorporate the contracts containing such a clause as appendices or indicate acceptance of the arbitration jurisdiction clause in those contracts. Although there might be some degree of correlation among these contracts, such correlation cannot negate their respective independence.

2. In accordance with the relevant provisions of the Arbitration Law, the parties must voluntarily reach an arbitration agreement to resolve disputes through arbitration; where no such agreement exists and one party applies for arbitration, the arbitration commission shall not accept the application. Therefore, the parties’ agreement on arbitration jurisdiction must be clearly expressed through the conclusion of an arbitration agreement, and an arbitration clause is legally binding only on the parties who have reached the arbitration agreement.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court
(2006) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 2

Appellants (Plaintiffs at First Instance): Suzhou Dongbao Real Estate Co., Ltd., domiciled at Room 102, No. 10, Tongjing North Road, Jinchang District, Suzhou, Jiangsu Province.
Legal Representative: You Jianqing, General Manager of the Company.

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Suzhou Jincheng Guarantee Co., Ltd., domiciled at Room 102, No. 10, Tongjing North Road, Jinchang District, Suzhou, Jiangsu Province.
Legal Representative: Xu Ada, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Suzhou Dongbao Metal Materials Co., Ltd., domiciled at Room 102, No. 10, Tongjing North Road, Jinchang District, Suzhou, Jiangsu Province.
Legal Representative: Xu Ada, General Manager of the Company.

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Suzhou Dongbao Ferrous Metal Materials Co., Ltd., domiciled at Taiping Industrial Park, Xiangcheng District, Suzhou, Jiangsu Province.
Legal Representative: Lu Rengen, General Manager of the Company.

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Xu Ada, male, born on October 18, 1957, Han ethnicity, residing at No. 1, Shijiantou, Suzhou, Jiangsu Province.

Respondents (Defendants at First Instance): Suzhou General Merchandise Corporation, domiciled at No. 330, Jingde Road, Suzhou, Jiangsu Province.
Legal Representative: Mao Jiasi, General Manager of the Corporation.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Jiangsu Girl's Spring Group, domiciled at No. 88, Xincun Middle Road, Jianghua Town, Taixing, Jiangsu Province.
Legal Representative: Cheng Yumin, General Manager of the Group.

For the dispute over asset transfer contract between appellants Suzhou Dongbao Real Estate Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Dongbao Company), Suzhou Jincheng Guarantee Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Guarantee Company), Suzhou Dongbao Metal Materials Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Metal Company), Suzhou Dongbao Ferrous Metal Materials Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Ferrous Metal Company), and Xu Ada and the respondents Suzhou General Merchandise Corporation (hereinafter referred to as Merchandise Corporation) and Jiangsu Girl's Spring Group (hereinafter referred to as Girl's Spring Company), the appellants, dissatisfied with the civil ruling (2005) Su Min Er Chu Zi No. 023-2 rendered by the Jiangsu High People's Court, appealed to this Court. This Court lawfully formed a collegiate panel composed of Presiding Judge Jin Jianfeng, Acting Judges Chen Bailing and Qian Xiaochen to hear the case. Court Clerk Yuan Hongxia served as recorder. The case is now concluded.

The court of first instance found upon review: On September 10, 2004, the Merchandise Corporation and an auction company entered into a "Jiangsu Province Entrusted Auction Contract", under which the Merchandise Corporation entrusted the auction company to auction Suzhou Bamianfeng Commercial Building Co., Ltd. Article 12 of that contract provided: "Any dispute arising from this contract shall be submitted to the Suzhou Arbitration Commission for arbitration." Subsequently, on December 28, 2004, Dongbao Company acquired Suzhou Bamianfeng Commercial Building Co., Ltd. through auction and signed and sealed the "Jiangsu Province Auction Transaction Confirmation Letter" (Type B), which stated that the Type B auction transaction confirmation letter applies only to the transaction between the auctioneer and the purchaser for a single auction item, and that any dispute shall be resolved by arbitration by the Suzhou Arbitration Commission. On December 28, 2004, the Merchandise Corporation, Girl's Spring Company, and Dongbao Company entered into a "Transfer Agreement" providing that the transfer payment to be made by Dongbao Company shall be paid into the bank account designated by the auction company. This agreement contained no arbitration clause and did not provide that it would be treated as an appendix to the "Jiangsu Province Entrusted Auction Contract" or the "Jiangsu Province Auction Transaction Confirmation Letter", nor did it contain any other such provision. Subsequently, in performing the agreement, Dongbao Company indeed transferred RMB 54.5 million as the transfer payment to the account designated by the auction company, which then transferred the sum to the Merchandise Corporation and Girl's Spring Company. Later, a dispute arose over the performance of the contract. On August 29, 2005, Dongbao Company, Guarantee Company, Metal Company, Ferrous Metal Company, and Xu Ada filed a lawsuit with the Jiangsu High People's Court, seeking an order that the Merchandise Corporation and Girl's Spring Company pay liquidated damages of RMB 10.9 million for delayed and incomplete performance of the contract; that the plaintiffs be permitted to suspend payment of the final installment of the equity transfer price of RMB 54.5 million; and that the litigation costs be borne by the Merchandise Corporation and Girl's Spring Company. During the defense period, the defendants Merchandise Corporation and Girl's Spring Company raised a jurisdictional objection, arguing that the case was essentially a dispute over an equity auction and should be arbitrated by the Suzhou Arbitration Commission, and therefore the plaintiffs' claim should be dismissed. On September 16, 2005, the Merchandise Corporation submitted an arbitration application to the Suzhou Arbitration Commission. On September 28, 2005, the Suzhou Arbitration Commission accepted the Merchandise Corporation's application.

The court of first instance held: The "Jiangsu Province Entrusted Auction Contract" between the Merchandise Corporation and the auction company contained an arbitration clause. The auction company publicly auctioned all equity interests in Suzhou Bamianfeng Commercial Building Co., Ltd. (with the Merchandise Corporation and Girl's Spring Company each holding 50% of the equity). On December 28, 2004, Dongbao Company won the bid and signed and sealed the "Jiangsu Province Auction Transaction Confirmation Letter", which also contained an arbitration clause. The above arbitration clauses clearly identified the arbitration institution and the use of arbitration to resolve disputes; these provisions did not violate any law or relevant regulation and should be deemed valid. The Merchandise Corporation, Girl's Spring Company, and Dongbao Company entered into a "Transfer Agreement" providing that the transfer payment from Dongbao Company to the Merchandise Corporation and Girl's Spring Company would be made through the auction company's account, and in performing the agreement, Dongbao Company indeed transferred RMB 54.5 million to the account designated by the auction company, which then transferred the amount to the Merchandise Corporation and Girl's Spring Company. In summary, the "Transfer Agreement" in this case was based on the entrusted auction contract and the transaction confirmation letter; without the entrusted auction contract and the transaction confirmation letter, there would be no "Transfer Agreement". The "Transfer Agreement" and the entrusted auction contract and the transaction confirmation letter formed a closely integrated whole that were interdependent; performance of the "Transfer Agreement" could not be separated from the entrusted auction contract and the transaction confirmation letter, nor could it be separated from the auction company. Furthermore, the "Transfer Agreement" between Dongbao Company, the Merchandise Corporation, and Girl's Spring Company did not exclude the arbitration clause in the auction transaction confirmation letter. Therefore, the claims of Dongbao Company, Guarantee Company, Metal Company, Ferrous Metal Company, and Xu Ada in this case should be subject to the arbitration clause in the "Jiangsu Province Auction Transaction Confirmation Letter". Accordingly, the claims of Dongbao Company did not meet the statutory conditions for filing a lawsuit. Pursuant to Article 111(2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court ruled: the claims of Dongbao Company, Guarantee Company, Metal Company, Ferrous Metal Company, and Xu Ada were dismissed.

Dongbao Company, Guarantee Company, Metal Company, Ferrous Metal Company, and Xu Ada, dissatisfied with this civil ruling, appealed to this Court, arguing: (1) There was no arbitration agreement between the parties in this case, and the ruling of first instance violated Article 4 of the Arbitration Law; (2) This case and the entrusted auction contract were different types of contracts, and the subject matter and legal relationship differed from those in the transaction confirmation letter; the ruling of first instance's conclusion that the parties in this case were bound by the arbitration clause in the transaction confirmation letter constituted an error in law application; (3) After the lawsuit was filed, the Merchandise Corporation and Girl's Spring Company submitted their defense and accepted judicial jurisdiction; the subsequent jurisdictional objection should not be entertained; (4) Before the plaintiffs filed the lawsuit, the defendant Merchandise Corporation and Girl's Spring Company had applied for preservation before trial with the Jiangsu High People's Court on the basis of the "Transfer Agreement" involved in this case, and the Jiangsu High People's Court lawfully granted preservation; it was ridiculous for them now to object to the court's jurisdiction; (5) The lawsuit was filed as a dispute over equity transfer, and the defendants' defense also concerned equity transfer; both parties acknowledged this, and the court of first instance's recharacterization as an asset transfer dispute lacked factual basis. In summary, they requested that the ruling of first instance be set aside, that the Jiangsu High People's Court be directed to hear the case lawfully and promptly, and that the Merchandise Corporation and Girl's Spring Company bear the litigation costs.

The Merchandise Corporation and Girl's Spring Company responded: (1) The court of first instance correctly found the facts of the case; (2) The court of first instance accurately characterized the relationship among the "Entrusted Auction Contract", the "Transaction Confirmation Letter", and the "Transfer Agreement"; the equity transfer was conducted through auction procedures; only after both parties had completed the transfer payment and delivery of the auction subject matter could the transaction confirmation letter be deemed fully performed; the equity "Transfer Agreement" was a component of performing the "Transaction Confirmation Letter" and should be regarded as a supplement and special agreement to the "Transaction Confirmation Letter"; therefore, disputes arising from the "Transfer Agreement" should be resolved in accordance with the method specified in the "Transaction Confirmation Letter"; (3) The appellants' grounds of appeal lacked legal basis; the "Transfer Agreement" could not exist independently; without the "Transaction Confirmation Letter", there would be no legal relationship between Dongbao Company and the Merchandise Corporation; the provisions in the "Transaction Confirmation Letter" covered all acts of the purchaser during the performance of the auction activities; thus, disputes arising from the performance of the "Transfer Agreement" should naturally be submitted to arbitration as provided in the "Transaction Confirmation Letter"; the equity transfer payment was also made by Dongbao Company into the auction company's account, which was also due to the existence of the transaction confirmation letter; this payment method further demonstrated that the "Transfer Agreement" was an implementation rule and supplementary clause of the "Transaction Confirmation Letter". In summary, although the "Transfer Agreement" did not directly contain an arbitration clause, it was a component of the "Transaction Confirmation Letter", serving to clarify and elaborate on the "Transaction Confirmation Letter"; together with the "Entrusted Auction Contract", it formed a closely integrated whole; the dispute arising from the "Transfer Agreement" was essentially a dispute arising from the "Transaction Confirmation Letter", and both governed the same legal relationship. They requested that the appeal be dismissed and the original ruling affirmed.

This Court further finds: On May 20, 2005, Guarantee Company, Metal Company, and Xu Ada jointly issued a "Letter of Guarantee" to the Merchandise Corporation, Girl's Spring Company, and the auction company, undertaking that Guarantee Company and Xu Ada would assume joint and several guarantor liability for Dongbao Company's obligation to pay the remaining portion of the equity transfer payment, and that Metal Company would provide as security the relevant real property land use rights certificates to be auctioned by the auction company.

On June 6, 2005, Dongbao Company, Metal Company, Ferrous Metal Company, and Guarantee Company jointly issued a "Request to Provide Mortgage Guarantee" to the Merchandise Corporation and Girl's Spring Company, undertaking that, in addition to the commitment of May 20, 2005 remaining unchanged, Metal Company and Ferrous Metal Company would each assume joint and several liability for Dongbao Company's obligation to pay the transfer payment.

This Court holds: The three contracts relevant to determining jurisdiction in this case are: the "Jiangsu Province Entrusted Auction Contract" between the Merchandise Corporation and the auction company, which contains an arbitration clause; the "Jiangsu Province Auction Transaction Confirmation Letter" between Dongbao Company and the auction company, which contains an arbitration clause; and the "Transfer Agreement" among the Merchandise Corporation, Girl's Spring Company, and Dongbao Company, which does not provide that it is an appendix to the other two contracts or that it accepts the arbitration jurisdiction of those two contracts, nor does it contain an arbitration clause. The parties to these three contracts are different, and the legal relationships formed are different. Although there is some correlation in the generation of these three contracts, such correlation cannot negate their respective independence. Dongbao Company, Guarantee Company, Metal Company, Ferrous Metal Company, and Xu Ada filed the lawsuit with the court of first instance based on the "Transfer Agreement". Because that transfer agreement contains no arbitration clause and does not accept the arbitration jurisdiction provisions of the other two contracts, and the five appellants expressly indicated that they do not accept arbitration jurisdiction, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Arbitration Law, parties must voluntarily reach an arbitration agreement to resolve disputes through arbitration; where no arbitration agreement exists and one party applies for arbitration, the arbitration commission shall not accept the application. It follows that the parties must clearly express their intention to agree on arbitration jurisdiction and conclude an arbitration agreement, and an arbitration clause is legally binding only on the parties who have reached the arbitration agreement and cannot bind persons outside the agreement. Therefore, for the lawsuit filed by the five appellants, Dongbao Company, Guarantee Company, Metal Company, Ferrous Metal Company, and Xu Ada, with the court on the basis of the "Transfer Agreement", the people's court has jurisdiction. As to the content of the "Transfer Agreement", the transaction price for the equity transfer was RMB 109 million, and the subject matter amount in this case exceeds RMB 50 million. In terms of subject-matter jurisdiction, it falls within the threshold for cases accepted by the Jiangsu High People's Court as approved by the Supreme People's Court. Accordingly, the Jiangsu High People's Court should accept this case in accordance with law.

In summary, the ruling of first instance correctly found the facts but improperly applied the law, and should be set aside. The appellants' appeal is well-founded and is supported by this Court. Pursuant to Article 152, paragraph 1, Article 153, paragraph 1(2), Article 154, and Article 158 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court rules as follows:

1. The civil ruling (2005) Su Min Er Chu Zi No. 023-2 of the Jiangsu High People's Court is set aside;
2. This case shall be accepted by the Jiangsu High People's Court.

The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 50, other fees of RMB 200, second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 50, and other fees of RMB 200 shall be jointly borne by Suzhou General Merchandise Corporation and Jiangsu Girl's Spring Group.

This ruling is final.

Presiding Judge: Jin Jianfeng
Acting Judge: Chen Bailing
Acting Judge: Qian Xiaochen

March 1, 2006

Court Clerk: Yuan Hongxia

Jin Jianfeng, Senior Judge: born in 1957, Doctor of Laws, appointed as Judge of the Supreme People's Court in 1997.
